To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a low power, low noise, high IIP3, small area, single stage CMOS LNA that can cover the entire 300 MHz to3 GHz band.
we present a single stage LNA with a small area, low NF, and a high IIP3.
a simple CMOS inverter-based LNA can be designed with a small area and a low power consumption while achieving a high IIP3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low noise, high gain and high IIP2 and IIP3 CMOS amplifiers.
the design, implementation and analysis of a 0.3 GHz to 3 GHz low noise amplifier with a high input third-order intercept point.
the design of a LNA with high HP3, low noise figure, low power consumption and small silicon area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this LNA is one of the best in terms of HP3 and one with the smallest silicon area.
the LNA presented in this paper has a good tradeoff between performance, silicon area and power consumption and is a good candidate for future wireless transceiver designs.
this amplifier is a good candidate for a wideband LNA with high linearity and good noise performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we achieved the best HP3 for a LNA in the same technology with the smallest area and the lowest power consumption.
we have designed an LNA with high HP3 that has a small silicon area.
this LNA is the smallest area, highest IIP3 and lowest NF in the 0.3 to 3 GHz range we could find.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple single stage amplifier can outperform more complex noise cancelling topologies in terms of NF and IIP3 while saving silicon area and power consumption.
a simple inverter based amplifier is enough to achieve high IIP3, low NF, good Sii and low power consumption, thus, reducing silicon area and power consumption.
a simple LNA with self-biased transistors can achieve better results than complex noise canceling architectures.
